@deskUpdAvailable.description: Sidebar notice, first line: a newer BT Wallet is out (the version is on the line under it).

@deskUpdDownload.description: Button and tooltip: download the newer version inside the app (it is installed after a restart).

@deskUpdOpensPage.description: Tooltip of the update notice when the app cannot install the update itself: a click opens the download page in the browser.

@deskUpdDownloading.description: Sidebar notice and Settings › About while the update downloads. {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100.

@deskUpdRestart.description: Button: close the app, install the downloaded update and open the app again.

@deskUpdReady.description: The update is downloaded and checked; it is installed by Restart to update.

deskUpdRestartHint: The app closes, installs it and opens again.

@deskUpdRestartHint.description: Settings › About, under '{version} is ready': what Restart to update does.

@deskUpdFailed.description: Sidebar notice and Settings › About: the download failed (the reason is in the tooltip or under it).

@deskUpdTryAgain.description: Second line of the notice and button: download the update again; it carries on from what already arrived.

@deskUpdInstallFailed.description: The downloaded update could not be started; the download page is offered instead.

@deskUpdOpenPage.description: Second line of the notice after a failed install: a click opens the download page in the browser.

deskUpdErrDamaged: The file did not match the signed update information.

@deskUpdErrDamaged.description: Why the download failed: wrong size or SHA-256. The file was deleted.

@deskUpdErrStopped.description: Why the download failed: the connection dropped. Trying again carries on from what arrived.

deskUpdErrInstall: The new version could not be put in place.

@deskUpdErrInstall.description: Why Restart to update failed: the installer could not be started or the app file could not be replaced.

deskUpdUnfinished: Update did not finish. Try again.

@deskUpdUnfinished.description: Sidebar notice and Settings › About (Windows): an update was started but Setup did not finish (it was stopped or failed part way); the action runs the update again. The version is on the line under it.

deskUpdManual: This copy cannot install updates itself.

@deskUpdManual.description: Slot tooltip and Settings › About › Updates: this copy (not an installed Windows copy, an AppImage in a folder it cannot write, a build folder, a .deb) cannot install the update itself; its actions open the download page instead.

@deskUpdDownloadInstall.description: Settings › About › Updates, button: download the newer version in the app; after it is checked, a restart installs it.

@deskUpdReadyTitle.description: Dialog title when the update the user started downloading is downloaded and checked; the sidebar slot names the version.

deskUpdReadyBody: The wallet locks and the app opens again.

@deskUpdReadyBody.description: Dialog text under 'Epic Cash {version} is ready': Restart now locks the wallet, closes the app, installs the update and opens the app again.

@deskUpdRestartNow.description: Dialog button: restart the app now to install the downloaded update.

@deskUpdLater.description: Dialog button: not now; 'Restart to update' stays in the sidebar and in Settings › About.

@deskUpdOpenDmg.description: macOS: button and sidebar line once the update's disk image is downloaded and checked: the app closes and the disk image opens in Finder (the app cannot install itself there).

deskUpdDmgHint: The app closes and the disk image opens: drag BT Wallet into Applications and replace the old one. Move Epic Cash Desktop, if it is there, to the Bin.

@deskUpdDmgHint.description: macOS: what happens and what to do, one line under the downloaded update and in its dialog. BT Wallet is the app's name and Epic Cash Desktop its name before (installs of 26.10.24 have that app); Applications and the Bin are the macOS folder and Trash (use their names in this language's macOS).

@deskUpdStripAct.description: The update strip's button at the top of the content area (one word): starts the download of the version the strip names, the same step as the sidebar's slot.

@deskUpdStripHide.description: The update strip's close button (×): its tooltip and screen-reader name. The strip stays away for this version and comes back for a newer one; the sidebar's slot stays.
